new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed and it was fully opened and confirmed silent. Spot-checks of the companion sources already held by the project for this glottocode: Loukotka 1968 (djvu text) has a general convention 'Stress: à é í ó ú' in its Introduction (line 1760, p. 36) but says nothing about stress in the Natú entry (p. 88), and its Natú forms carry only one such mark (barí, tobacco) plus length colons, so no placement rule can be read off; Lima Neto & Nunes 2022 pp. 414-415 (the text) list the 'acentos tônicos' (acute, circumflex, macron, tilde) purely as graphemes of the Xokó/Natú transcriptions with no statement of where stress falls; Loukotka 1955 and Meader 1978 have no accent/stress vocab…

new_statements.quote: Além dos vocabulários acima, levantados pelo Dr. Carlos Estêvam, prático no trato dos índios, possuimos mais 3 colhidos no sertão pernambucano, mas por coletor inculto, porém possuido de muito boa vontade. Para facilitar a comparação adotamos a ortografia e os sinais diacriticos usados pelo Dr. Carlos Estêvam, isto é, as convenções seguintes: Acento agudo para a tônica [sign lost in scanned] sílaba longa / sinal indicando palavra sincopada. Sh igual a x
new_statements.translation: Besides the vocabularies above, taken down by Dr. Carlos Estêvam, experienced in dealing with the Indians, we have three more collected in the Pernambuco backlands, but by an uneducated though very willing collector. To ease comparison we adopted the spelling and the diacritic signs used by Dr. Carlos Estêvam, that is, the following conventions: acute accent for the tonic [stressed syllable]; [sign] long syllable; / sign indicating a syncopated word; Sh equals [Portuguese] x.
new_statements.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1958. Línguas tapuias desconhecidas do Nordeste (alguns vocabulários inéditos). Boletim de Antropologia (Fortaleza: Universidade do Ceará, Serviço de Antropologia) 2(1): 3-19. Natú = Vocabulário nº 4, p. 13.
new_statements.locator: Paragraph immediately after Vocabulário nº 5 (Chocó) and the summary 'Êstes vocabulários tem 115 palavras.. 4º de índios Natú 17..', i.e. pp. 13-14 by position (Natú list itself: Vocabulário nº 4, p. 13); exact page not visible in Google snippets. Identical text in both scanned copies (n4agYGND1aoC, ATrv3L_0d2sC).
new_statements.relation_note: States the transcription key for Estevão's five 1940 vocabularies (Brejo dos Padres, Serra Negra, Tushá, Natú, Chocó): the acute accent marks the stressed syllable ('acento agudo para a tônica'), another sign marks a long syllable, '/' a syncopated word, sh = Portuguese x. No rule of stress placement is stated. Applied to the Natú list (Estrêla Iroinkó, Fogo Shakishá, Água Kraunã, Rio S. Francisco Opára, Cachimbo Katuká, Cachimbo cerimonial Kuzipé, Maracá Shishiá, Dinheiro Meré, Mulher Pikwá, Gente estranha Zitók, Boi Krazó, Ovelha Sêprun, Jacaré Gozê, Jaboti Kati, Mandioca Grogó, Feijão Ma/tsaká, Tabaco Bazé): 13 of 17 forms bear an acute, 12 of them on the final syllable and 1 on the penu…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Not a rule from the author: under the stated key (acute = stressed syllable) the marked Natú forms are stressed on the final syllable in 12 of 13 cases (one penult, Opára). Read as predominantly final stress in a 17-word remembered vocabulary; low evidential weight.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated by the author; in the data Opára (Rio São Francisco) is penult-marked; four items unmarked.
new_statements.identity_note: The primary publication of Carlos Estevão's 1940 Natú list ('Palavras colhidas de caboclos "Natu", em Colégio, Alagoas', 17 items) that Loukotka 1968, Meader 1978 and Lima Neto & Nunes 2022 cite at p. 13; our bibliography has it as print-only/unlocated. New here: two library scans are full-text indexed in Google Books (no full view), which also means a HathiTrust search-only copy from UFL/Cornell is likely; and the article states Estevão's diacritic conventions, which none of the reproductions (Loukotka, Wikipedia, Lima Neto & Nunes) carried over.
